knowledge.subject: Monkey D. Luffy

identity.name: Monkey D. Luffy
identity.continuity: One Piece manga through the end of Wano Country arc
identity.explanation: The three technique pages explicitly identify Monkey D. Luffy as their user and provide manga chapter references for his abilities. The Wano synopsis independently identifies Luffy, his Gear 5 victory over Kaidou, and his subsequent Emperor status. These are substantive descriptions of the requested character, not merely navigation links. Only material supported within the requested manga period is consolidated; adaptation-only and later developments are excluded.

claims.text: Luffy belongs to the Straw Hat crew. During Wano, he promises Tama a country where she can eat her fill every day, joins the raid on Onigashima, defeats Kaidou after manifesting Gear 5, and departs with his crew. By the arc's conclusion, his bounty has risen to 3 billion berries and he has become one of the Four Emperors.

His defining combat style combines rubber-body stretching and recoil with punches, kicks, body launches, grappling, inflation, speed-enhancing Gears, and Haki. Gear 5 adds highly improvisational body deformation and rubberization of his surroundings.

His Devil Fruit is commonly called the Gomu Gomu no Mi; the Gear 5 page identifies its underlying identity as the Mythical Zoan Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika. It gives him a rubber body, including rubber organs and blood vessels, and its awakening strengthens and greatly expands the freedom of that rubber physiology.

Luffy uses Armament Haki to harden and strengthen attacking limbs and to reinforce defenses. By Wano he uses advanced Armament Haki and Supreme King Haki infusion to damage Kaidou. Bajrang Gun specifically employs outward Haki emission to strike without direct physical contact.

Gear 2, also called Gear Two or Gear Second, increases blood flow to supply more oxygen and nutrients, enhancing speed, mobility, and striking power. His rubber organs and vessels withstand the accelerated circulation. It debuted in his manga fight against Blueno; he developed it after encountering Aokiji and observing CP9's Soru.

Before the timeskip, Gear 2 required leg pumping and affected his whole body, with rapidly evaporating sweat producing steam. After the timeskip he can activate it through individual limbs and use short, controlled bursts for individual attacks without his original stance.

Gear 2 consumes extra oxygen, nutrients, and energy, causing hunger, panting, and eventually reduced performance or severe exhaustion; prolonged early use left him unable to move. Food replenishes his depleted nutrients. Lucci warns that the strain may shorten Luffy's lifespan, but the page does not establish a quantified or independently confirmed lifespan loss. Later mastery reduces the observed burden.
Soru, translated as Shave: Gear 2 enables Luffy to reproduce the Six Powers high-speed movement technique, disappearing from ordinary view; the page describes his proficiency as surpassing Blueno's.

Gomu Gomu no Jet Pistol is an extremely fast straight punch whose fist movement is invisible; Jet Stamp is the corresponding forward kick. Gomu Gomu no Jet Bullet instead emphasizes an extremely fast, powerful close-range punch with nearly simultaneous stretching and snapback.

Gomu Gomu no Jet Bazooka is a high-speed charging double open-palm strike, used to overcome Blueno's Tekkai 'Go'; it can also propel Luffy in midair during repeated attacks. Gomu Gomu no Twin Jet Pistol instead strikes simultaneously with two clenched fists.

Gomu Gomu no Jet Whip is a sweeping kick so fast that only its slipstream is visible. Gomu Gomu no Jet Gatling is a rapid punch barrage leaving jet streams in place of visible arms; it defeated Rob Lucci. Its high energy demand limits sustained use. Luffy also performs an omnidirectional version while lying on his back against the Boa sisters.

Gomu Gomu no Jet Rocket uses stretched arms anchored to something to propel Luffy forward at high speed. Gomu Gomu no Jet Migawari, translated as Human Shield Jet or Jet Human Shield, rapidly pulls another person into an incoming attack's path; Luffy used Buggy to intercept Mihawk's attack.

Gomu Gomu no Jet Hammer wraps Luffy's legs around a target and rapidly smashes them into the ground, without the original Hammer's twisting and untwisting in the manga. Jet Mace is a high-speed spinning kick while falling. Jet Spear is the accelerated version of his Yari/Spear attack, used on the floor during his fight with Monet.

Gomu Gomu no Red Hawk combines Gear 2 and Armament hardening with a stretched-back arm that ignites before delivering a flaming punch. Its impact produces a fiery explosion, even underwater, and burns the target. Its supported manga debut here is against Hody Jones; during Wano, Kaidou dodges it.

Gomu Gomu no Hawk Gatling is Armament-hardened Jet Gatling, initially named Buso Koka: Gomu Gomu no Jet Gatling before receiving the Hawk name against Doflamingo. Hawk Rifle is a Gear 2, Armament-hardened twisting punch whose rotation increases its force.

Gomu Gomu no Eagle Bazooka is the Armament-enhanced Jet Bazooka, stretching both hardened arms backward before striking forward. Hawk Whip is an elongated sweeping kick with a hardened leg. Hawk Stamp is a hardened forward sole strike that leaves a sandal imprint.

Gear 3, also called Gear Three or Gear Third, enlarges body parts by blowing air into the bones through a bitten thumb opening. Luffy can transfer this air through his torso into different limbs. Enlarged bones provide giant-scale striking force and a hard, firm defense, unlike the soft, squishy inflation of ordinary Gomu Gomu no Fusen.

Gear 3's early drawbacks are reduced mobility, vulnerability to fast opponents or confined spaces, and delay when shifting air between limbs. Exhaling ends the form and can propel Luffy backward. Before the timeskip, deactivation also caused temporary shrinking for approximately the duration of its use, with severely reduced strength and little or no stretching ability.

After the timeskip, Luffy no longer shrinks after Gear 3. He controls inflation size and concentrates air nearer his fists and wrists, leaving more of his arms mobile for faster extension and withdrawal. He combines inflation with Armament Haki; a smaller inflated, hardened arm can function as a shield, including against Fujitora's slashes.

Hone Fusen, or Bone Balloon, is Gear 3's bone-inflation technique. It provides a firmer defense than ordinary Balloon, causing bullets to ricochet. The Gear 3 version of Gomu Gomu no Rocket launches Luffy with inflated chest bones and retains that bullet-ricocheting defense; it is not named a Gigant attack.

Gomu Gomu no Gigant Pistol is an enlarged-fist punch powerful enough to launch Lucci despite his Tekkai defense. Gigant Axe raises an enlarged leg and brings it down on the target. Gigant Whip transfers inflation into a leg for a powerful roundhouse kick.

Gomu Gomu no Gigant Bazooka inflates both arms for a giant double-palm strike and was used to defeat Oars. Gigant Rifle delivers an enlarged twisting, drilling punch and provided the finishing blow against PX-4.

Gomu Gomu no Gigant Stamp is a straight kick with an inflated leg; Luffy used it with Mr. 3's Giant Candle Wall against Magellan. An unnamed Armament- and Supreme King-enhanced version appears against Kaidou. Gigant Fusen enlarges his torso into a sturdier giant balloon, cushioning Sengoku's attack to protect Ace and Mr. 3.

Gomu Gomu no Gigant Jet Shell combines Gear 2's speed with Gear 3's bone-inflated torso, launching Luffy like a giant cannonball. It defeated Shadow's Asgard-enhanced Gecko Moria, but its early use compounded Gear 2's metabolic strain with Gear 3's mobility problems. The pages report that after Udon training he can combine Gears 2 and 3 without the earlier repercussions.

Gomu Gomu no Elephant Gun is an Armament-hardened Gigant Pistol with inflation concentrated at the fist and wrist for improved mobility and recoil. Elephant Gatling repeatedly strikes with two inflated, hardened fists, keeping the upper arms comparatively mobile for rapid withdrawal and follow-up punches.

Gomu Gomu no Grizzly Magnum combines Elephant Gun's enlarged hardened arms with Bazooka's two-arm strike: Luffy approaches with his arms stretched behind him, leaps, and drives them forward. It defeated Caesar Clown. Thor Elephant Gun is an Elephant Gun surrounded by electric sparks, used as a descending strike to defeat Chinjao and restore his pointed head.

Gomu Gomu no Gigant Tsuppari, translated as Giant Sumo Slap, stretches an arm backward and inflates it as it shoots forward into a giant open-palm strike. It knocked Urashima out of the ring and through buildings.

Gomu Gomu no Red Roc combines Elephant Gun and Red Hawk: Gear 3 enlarges the fist while Gear 2 and advanced Armament Haki produce a huge flaming hardened punch. It knocked down, burned, and injured Kaidou, unlike Luffy's earlier ineffective attacks.

Gomu Gomu no Roc Gun enhances Elephant Gun with Supreme King Haki infusion in addition to Armament hardening and inflation. Roc Gatling combines inflated fists, Armament hardening, Supreme King infusion, and Gear 2 speed for a barrage able to match Kaidou's attacks in his Human-Beast Form.

The supplied pages establish Gear 4 as an earlier form using muscle inflation. The Gear 5 page identifies Boundman's limb compression for enhanced blows and Tankman's offensive use of defense, and identifies Over Kong Gun as the Gear 4 antecedent of Bajrang Gun. These references provide only partial coverage of Gear 4.

Gear 5, also called Gear Five or Gear Fifth, is Luffy's awakened Nika-fruit form, first achieved during the final Onigashima battle with Kaidou in chapter 1044. His hair and clothing turn white, his eyebrows become swirled, clouds surround his neck and arms, and his heartbeat takes on the rhythm called the Drums of Liberation. He becomes notably joyful, laughing, and creatively playful.

Gear 5 increases strength, speed, durability, and rubber-body freedom beyond Luffy's previous forms. During Wano he can enlarge limbs or his entire body without first pumping air into them, grab and swing Kaidou's dragon body, and run through midair by spinning his legs rapidly. The page also associates his unconscious recovery at awakening with awakened Zoan recovery.

Gear 5's cartoonishly malleable body can wrap around Kaidou's spiked club or flatten under an impact and return to shape. This mitigates damage rather than eliminating it: attacks still hurt and can injure him, and he remains vulnerable to cutting attacks.

Gear 5 extends rubber properties to terrain and other bodies. During Wano, Luffy uses rubberized ground to cushion impacts and redirects Kaidou's Bolo Breath with a stretched section of roof. His blows stretch Kaidou's body while still transferring striking force. He can also rubberize and grab lightning.

Gear 5 is taxing and can lapse, leaving Luffy visibly exhausted and aged-looking. The page's Wano reference to chapter 1045 supports restarting the form by forcing his heartbeat back into the Drums of Liberation rhythm and pushing onward despite exhaustion; no precise duration or numerical stamina cost is established.

Gomu Gomu no Fusen in Gear 5 is a highly buoyant Balloon variation, first used inside Kaidou. Gomu Gomu no Gigant, translated as Gum-Gum Giant, enlarges Luffy's entire body to giant size rather than inflating only one limb.

Gomu Gomu no Bajrang Gun is Gear 5's enormous version of Over Kong Gun. Luffy enlarges his fist to nearly Onigashima's size and infuses advanced Armament and Supreme King Haki, emitting Haki to avoid direct contact. It is his culminating Wano attack and defeats Kaidou.

Gomu Gomu no Dasshutsu Rocket, translated as Escape Rocket, follows Balloon inside Kaidou: Luffy stretches his arms through Kaidou's eyes, grabs his nose, and launches himself out. Gomu Gomu no Nawatobi, translated as Jump Rope, follows Gigant and uses Kaidou's dragon body as a skipping rope.

Gomu Gomu no Kaminari, translated as Lightning, gives a lightning bolt rubber properties so Luffy can grab and throw it at Kaidou. The manga-supported technique is distinct from the page's anime-only elaboration involving multiple bolts.

The Gear 5 page identifies an enlarged, spinning, Haki-enhanced hook against Kaidou in chapter 1045 as an earlier unnamed instance of the attack later called Gomu Gomu no Star Gun. The Wano action is supported, but that later name and the Kizaru-specific effects are not treated as established within this record's cutoff.
